correctness.rationale: The sourced {2}-LID recurrence is checked in the complete motivating primary text. Exact disjoint-path independent-set counts yield D_j, the recurrence gives sum_{i<=n-3} a_i=a_n-4, and every representation of m<a_n uses indices <n. These imply the finite bounds. Normalizing by the unique positive rho satisfying rho^-1+rho^-3=1 makes the recurrence a positive convex combination and proves a_n=Theta(rho^n). Binet Fibonacci growth gives D_j=Theta(phi^j), proving the strict exponential mean rate. The accompanying verifier independently checks finite mex construction and complete sums through index 17; finite checks are not used to infer the infinite claim.

value.rationale: Question 5 in the motivating S-LID paper asks for the growth of average legal-decomposition counts; S={2} is the first non-Fibonacci singleton forbidden-distance case, already separately analyzed for its recurrence. The result determines a previously unspecified exact mean exponential growth constant and gives strong finite all-index Fibonacci-product inequalities, exhibiting a genuine entropy-versus-arithmetic-growth gap. It does not claim general-case resolution or a limiting prefactor.
